approved_composition_prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create a revised, DENSER rough isometric architectural composition sketch based on reference image 1 (the previous neighborhood sketch). This is a layout iteration for discussion, NOT a polished final artwork. Preserve its graphite construction lines, loose pencil contours, very light pale-blue washes, white paper, elevated isometric angle, blue-striped single-storey proposed cafe and small parking area. Change the GEOGRAPHY and DENSITY substantially as specified below. One continuous coherent neighborhood, not panels.

Screen-space layout is essential:
BACK LEFT / UPPER LEFT: a dense residential society of FIVE tall apartment towers of varied height (8–15 floors), grouped close enough to communicate many households, shared gate, a compact central garden, connecting paths. Tallest masses at far back left, all contained in frame. A few low residential buildings at their street edge add depth. Towers must not cover the central proposed cafe.
TOP RIGHT / UPPER RIGHT: a cluster of THREE medium-height office buildings, 5–8 floors, different simple block masses, one shared arrival court, clearly a workplace district. Keep offices shorter than residential skyline. This replaces the former single isolated office.
CENTER: the bustling existing pedestrian area, a continuous sidewalk/plaza and street intersection, visibly busier than elsewhere with loose tiny walking figures, a small roadside kiosk, crossings, a few cars and scooters. Make this plausible Indian urban street context without cluttering every surface.
METRO: place an UNDERGROUND METRO ENTRANCE directly BESIDE this bustling area, in the MIDDLE RIGHT of the composition, below the office cluster, near the main intersection and proposed cafe. Draw open stairwell descending into ground with handrails, small canopy and blue M sign. Pedestrians visibly flow from its stairs along the busy sidewalk past the proposed cafe, rather than gathering at its door. Metro should feel integrated with this busy street, not detached at the far edge of the map. No elevated railway.
PROPOSED CAFE: near the CENTER-LOWER part of the neighborhood, at the main street corner, dominant blue-striped awning, vacant candidate storefront with broad windows. Preserve a small adjoining parking court to its right with TWO car bays, one car, a separate scooters/bicycles strip, continuous pedestrian sidewalk and clear entry path. Not a successful operating cafe full of seated patrons.
BOTTOM / FOREGROUND: add a separate clearly visible row of THREE existing competing cafe / bakery storefronts across the street from the proposed cafe and nearer the viewer. These are at the BOTTOM of the composition, NOT the old upper-left shop row. Low-rise 1–2 storey buildings, different awnings, a few outdoor tables and existing seated customers. Keep them secondary in contrast, only pale blue/gray, so the proposed cafe is still the anchor. Show a real street and crossing separating proposed site from competitors. Do not obscure the proposed cafe with foreground roofs.
Increase density by closer coherent blocks and more purposeful buildings and pedestrians, not by filling the entire image with tree texture. Planting consists of simplified round tree masses, small shrubs and street trees, subordinate to architecture. Keep street widths believable, connected network, no disconnected roads. Full neighborhood with modest white margins, landscape composition, all buildings visible.

Annotations: small handwritten margin callouts with thin pencil leader lines, accurately pointing to their districts: 'Residential society' at back left, 'Offices' at top right, 'Metro entrance' at middle right, 'Proposed cafe' to the blue awning site, 'Parking' to its small court, 'Existing cafes' to the bottom foreground row. A thin dashed BLUE perspective outline around only the proposed cafe / parking / immediate busy corner marks 'Opening view', excluding metro, towers, offices and competitors from that footprint. This boundary is a storyboard camera-footprint annotation, not a wall/fence. Small title at top: 'DENSER NEIGHBORHOOD — LAYOUT SKETCH'.
Keep text sparse and legible. No data cards, no statistics, no UI.
Style: intentionally unfinished rough concept sketch, visible perspective guide lines, restrained facade marks, loose graphite hatching, white paper. Less surface detail than the supplied reference: don't labor over every window, leaf or car. No glossy rendering, no final polished 3D, no photorealism, no decorative dense vegetation, no giant cartoon people, no claims that the site will succeed.
storyboard_prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Make a FIVE-BEAT ROUGH STORYBOARD SHEET for GeoMarketeer, continuing exactly the approved neighborhood composition in reference image 1. It is a storyboard for review, not a polished illustration or final interface. Portrait sheet, five generous horizontal rows, each row has a pencil sketch frame occupying left 60% and legible typeset editorial copy on white to the right 40%. Thin subtle row dividers, tiny numbered step label. White background, graphite pencil, occasional restrained pale blue. No cartoon protagonist, no comic speech bubbles.

REFERENCE AUTHORITY: image 1 is the LOCKED GEOGRAPHY. Do not redesign it. Tall apartment group back left, office group top right, underground metro entrance middle right next to the busy pedestrian street, candidate cafe with blue-striped awning at center and small parking court immediately to its right, existing competing cafe row at the bottom across the street. Keep their shapes, street intersection, orientation and relative locations consistent in EVERY frame. Use camera crops and widening views of this ONE neighborhood. Do not invent or move a candidate unit into the foreground competitor row. Sid's proposed site is the SAME blue-striped single-storey unit across the road from those competitors in every beat. No new alternative site, no move to a supposedly better location, no before/after cafe business success. Treat any furniture in the candidate unit as placeholder; no customers seated there.
Opening camera is now revised to include the bottom competing-cafe row AND candidate site across the road. The old dashed 'Opening view' annotation on source image is a previous camera guide, not geography: omit that annotation in the storyboard. Keep all real buildings and roads.

Top title verbatim: 'GEOMARKETEER — FIVE-CLICK STORY'
Small subtitle verbatim: 'One locked neighborhood. A wider understanding.'
Rows:

01 — THE OPPORTUNITY
SKETCH: close crop of the existing bottom-row cafes with some occupied terrace tables and people on the sidewalk. Include a glimpse of the same vacant blue-awning candidate unit across the road near top of this crop so the relationship is established. Apartment towers, offices and metro outside crop. A small understated pointer to candidate site, no big Sid illustration.
COPY headline verbatim: 'The cafés here were busy.'
COPY support verbatim: 'Sid saw a promising place to open his own.'
Small camera note: 'Start with the existing café cluster.'

02 — THE ASSUMPTION
SKETCH: widen slightly to clearly frame the existing cafe row, road crossing and proposed blue-awning cafe with its small parking court. Crowd visible passing through the street; candidate remains empty. Gently emphasize candidate awning blue. Do not imply competition means failure.
COPY headline verbatim: 'Surely there was room for one more?'
COPY support verbatim: 'A busy café cluster made the location feel like a safe bet.'
Small camera note: 'Connect the busy cafés to Sid’s proposed site.'

03 — THE REVEAL
SKETCH: camera pulls to the RIGHT and a little back, keeping the same candidate cafe as anchor while revealing the underground metro stairwell and canopy beside the bustling street. Several tiny commuters emerge and walk ALONG the pavement past the candidate unit. They do not all enter cafes. Apartment and office groups still only partial or faint edges.
COPY headline verbatim: 'Passing through isn’t the same as stopping.'
COPY support verbatim: 'The metro explained some of the crowd. It didn’t tell Sid who would buy.'
Small camera note: 'Reveal the metro and the pedestrian route.'

04 — THE CONTEXT
SKETCH: pull fully back to the approved ENTIRE map: clustered tall residences upper left, office cluster upper right, metro middle right, proposed cafe and parking center, existing cafes bottom. SAME geography from reference. Add just three small area-level annotation labels with fine leader lines, NOT cards hovering over individual people: 'People: residents, workers, age groups'; 'Spending: income, spending patterns'; 'Competition: existing cafés, offers'. No statistics or inferred personal data, no ranked zones, no recommendations. These represent questions/data categories, not measured results.
COPY headline verbatim: 'He needed more than footfall.'
COPY support verbatim: 'Who lives and works nearby? What do they spend? What do the existing cafés already offer?'
Small camera note: 'Reveal the wider neighborhood and the questions it raises.'

05 — THE RESPONSE
SKETCH: same full approved neighborhood and SAME proposed cafe site, slightly quieter drawing, restrained blue emphasis on candidate and soft subtle link to the three context categories. No new site, no moving or morphing of buildings, no fabricated success outcome. Bottom competitors remain visible. A modest GeoMarketeer wordmark outside sketch okay.
COPY headline verbatim: 'Same corner. A clearer picture.'
COPY support verbatim: 'GeoMarketeer helps businesses understand a neighborhood before choosing where to open.'
Small text verbatim: 'My role: UX Research & Interaction Design'
Small camera note: 'End the story. Optional exploration follows.'

Visual execution: sketch frames deliberately less detailed than source reference. Simple architectural masses, sparse facade marks and loose tree crowns, tiny gestural figures, rough pencil construction strokes; preserve the map positions rather than polishing details. Editorial copy clean, highly readable, not handwritten scribbles. No repeated full map in the first three rows: camera framing should visibly progress from nearby competition to candidate site to metro to full neighborhood. Five rows exactly. No demographic numbers, claims of verified business performance, fictional success story, large icons, dense UI panels or final rendered materials.
storyboard_correction_prompt: Edit this storyboard sheet with ONE precise correction, preserving all text verbatim, the five-row layout, all other four illustration panels and the rough pencil style. In ROW 02 ONLY (THE ASSUMPTION), tighten the camera crop of the left-hand sketch so it frames the proposed cafe, its parking, the street crossing and existing cafes, with the metro entrance entirely outside the right edge of the frame. The M sign, canopy, stairwell and metro itself MUST NOT be visible anywhere in row 02. This is a camera crop of the same geography, not removal of the metro from the neighborhood. The metro must remain fully visible in row 03 (THE REVEAL), row 04 and row 05 exactly as it is now. Do not change row 01, any copy, labels, typography or the approved building locations. This change protects the narrative reveal: viewers first discover the metro in row 03. Keep the whole full five-row storyboard sheet in the output, same proportions and framing.
